title: Ignition timing, coils, plugs and knock control
whatItIs: Ignition must start combustion at the right crank angle. The ECU can remove timing to protect the engine from knock, heat or bad fuel; the ignition system can also fail under cylinder pressure.
normalValues: Timing depends heavily on load, RPM, temperature and fuel. A healthy graph does not show timing collapsing repeatedly under normal load without a reason.
deviations: Late timing under load reduces torque even when airflow and fuel are normal
Misfires under boost or WOT often expose weak coils or excessive plug gap
High IAT/coolant or low octane can create knock retard
Electrical noise or voltage drop can imitate ignition faults
influence: The driver experiences ignition faults as hesitation, surging, low power, pinging or flashing MIL. The app must separate ignition energy loss from mixture and mechanical loss.
checks: Compare timing at equal load/RPM before and after symptom
Inspect plugs, gap, coils, boots and grounds
Verify fuel octane and thermal conditions before blaming knock sensors
